title: Shorty: musicians' name for whiskey, and Watts playing high at the California
summary: Watts and Alfred explain that Shorty means liquor and tell of Watts coming to work at George's club drunk.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Let's see, this is a reel for Bob Watts, February 28th, 1963. And you were talking about your good friend Shorty, who was that? Talking about Shorty?
Yeah, yeah, he ain't the good friend, man. Shorty knows, Shorty's bad. Shorty'll tell ya. Shorty'll tell ya.
Some people don't know who Shorty is.
No, no, they don't know what we're talking about.

We always say that. Yeah, the cats get Shorty, they blow it out a bottle, ya know. Yeah, they don't know who Shorty is. Yeah, and they drink it, you know, and food will just think they can play better. Like I used to be weak to that effect. Oh, you get a little shorty, man, you can really blow. That's right, make you believe it. Yeah, and man, you'll be playing loud and raw. I used to go up on Alpha's job when he was at the California, when I was working with him. See, that's after the Lewis's Cafe. I worked with him quite a while there. Yeah, about three years. See, he was an M.G. of the job. About how long, Gabe? About three years. Yeah, and I used to go up there high, you know, some nights, you know. You know, and I'd tell him. Like the Lord, it's 64 and I. Or Alpha's, yeah, you come again with your head charged. He said, all day long to have your fun and then you come on the job like that. Wait till tonight. I'd say, that's all right, man, I can blow. I'd say, all right, Laffette, give me your head. Nah, that's all right. All right, kick your band off, Gabe. I'd tell Alpha, kick your band off. And he's smoking up there. He's setting up a little high for me, you know. But he'll go ahead and let me work. If I could work, I'll go ahead and work. One night he made me mad.
